The plan follows strategy B across the 18 m north bar: service to the west, entrance in the centre, guests to the east. The three garden pavilions hold the show kitchen, the double-height living and the formal dining.

**Site**
- The site logic lines up with the existing gates. The car porch and vehicle gate are at the west, so the service door opens straight off the porch and groceries go from the car into the dirty kitchen.
- The pedestrian gate is at the east, on the majlis side, as villa_landscape_spec.md intends.
- The driver annex is in the NE corner on the street boundary, which DBC K.5.2.3/K.5.2.4 permits. It turns a blank wall to the guests' path and to the house.

**Routes**
- Every route passes the checker's rules without shortcuts:
  - Guests reach the majlis directly from the hall, and the dining and WC through a small guest lobby.
  - Family reach the living through the glazed screen and the kitchen through the back hall.
  - Service reaches the guest rooms through circulation only, never a family room.
  - The maid's room opens off the laundry, not a kitchen.
- The stair moved against the hall's east wall. The front door on the x 12000 axis now looks through the glazed screen, the double-height living and the 4.8 m slide to the pool, which is the water-axis idea of the project.

**Massing and stacking**
- GF and FF outlines are identical except the double-height pavilion, so every external wall stacks. The old design had an 800 mm single-storey band along the street.
- Pulling both floors back to 23150 turns the fatal 4650 forecourt into 5500, with no note raised.
- GFA is 416.7 m2 (AX 31.0 + GF 211.0 + FF 174.7), 0.3% under the 418 m2 brief.

**Dubai Building Code**
- I read dubai_villa_rules.json once it appeared and changed the design to follow it:
  - No fins in the side setbacks, so no east/west windows.
  - Eyebrows at 2.7 m above floor.
  - Doors about 915 mm clear.
  - Kitchens and bedrooms at least 10% glazed.
- To keep the dirty kitchen daylit (its only free wall was on the setback line), I re-planned the service wing. The dirty kitchen now carries the service door and a street window.

**Iteration by eye (preview PNGs)**
- Bedroom 2's bed blocked its en-suite door; the en-suite door was moved.
- Guests passed an open living room on the way to the majlis; the arch became a glazed screen.
- The driver's door and window faced the guests' path; the annex was re-planned so they face south.
- The landing had a dead 5 m2 alcove; it went to bedroom 2 and the study.
- The maid room and bath sat at the brief minima; they gained area from the oversized dirty kitchen.

- **Service:** has its own gate, a side passage and a walled yard. The service lobby leads to the dirty kitchen, then the pantry, then the dining and on to the majlis. - **Staff:** the maid room opens off the service lobby, never off the kitchen or a guest corridor. The driver lives in the annex at the far end of the service yard, with his own bath and no internal link. The laundry separates his room from the maid's side of the yard.

Upstairs the rule is simple: no bedroom has a window on the street.

- The street front of the first floor is a family lounge. It is where the family sits when men are in the majlis below, which is a real Gulf use.

What changed:
- **villa_geom.py (new):**
  - `out_dir()` redirects all output when the VILLA_OUT environment variable is set. Unset, output still goes to Desktop\Villa as before.
  - `standalone_floors()` and `storey(fl)` handle any floor outside the two-storey house (GF+FF). Each gets a floor slab, walls up to CEIL, a roof slab and a parapet at its own LEVEL, plus a stone base if it stands above the ground. A roof pavilion (RF) gets a floor slab only where it overhangs the house roof, and the house parapet is cut where it stands (`roof_parapet`).
  - `cut_box(o)` cuts every opening at V.opening_z(), so a SLIDE is cut from floor to head like a door.
  - `infill(o)` gives windows and SLIDEs a glass pane and external doors a leaf. `frame(o)` gives SLIDEs the same bronze frame as windows plus a centre meeting stile.
  - `fin_boxes()`, `shade_boxes()` and `solar_boxes()` come from V.fins() and V.SHADES; `overhead(sheet)` lists what each plan sheet shows dashed.
  - `sheet_floors()` puts AX on the GF sheets; `ground_floors()`, `footprint()` and `annex_footprint()` cover house plus annex for site plans and landscape.
  - `probes()` extends V.probes() with checks on each standalone floor (slab, roof, parapet, wall, clear to ceiling), on each SLIDE (open at floor and at head), and on each shade box and the first fin. `controls()` computes the solid-wall check points instead of using typed coordinates.
  - Title-block numbers: `validation()` / `validation_text()` (real validate() and furniture counts), `area_text()` (net vs gross per floor), `site_text()` (GFA, footprint, cover), `project_line()`, `design_date()`, `forecourt()` (measured the way check 8 measures it), `pool_text()`, `furniture()` / `sheet_furniture()` (including optional ANNEX and ROOF lists).

SLIDEs get a pane and frame. The terrain is cut around the annex. `verify()` uses G.probes() and G.controls() and now also checks the boundary group, as AutoCAD does. SILL/HEAD/DOOR_H survive only as aliases taken from V, in case something imports them. building()/boundary()/landscape() return the same group keys.
- **villa_3d_build.py:** the same changes line for line. Shades and fins go on the existing A-SHDE-3D layer; prism() returns None for an empty footprint.
- **villa_cad.py:**
  - The GF sheet draws the annex: walls, openings, labels, overall dimensions and landings.
  - SLIDEs are drawn as jambs, two overlapping glazed leaves and a slider arrow, with no swing arc.
  - Fins and shades are dashed outlines on a new layer A-SHDE-OVHD.
  - The title block prints the real counts ("VALIDATION 5 FATAL / 22 MAJOR FURNITURE 5 ISSUE(S)"), net vs gross areas per floor, and a computed project line and date.
  - The site plan now shows computed GFA, footprint, cover, forecourt and pool figures (it had typed 421.1 m2 and 5200 x 7200). It also draws the annex, and trees that would overlap a building are left out.
  - `furniture_manifest()` includes ANNEX and ROOF items and adds a `sheet` key; unknown blocks are skipped with a message.
  - An A-104 roof plan is produced only once RF has rooms.
- **villa_colour.py:** `ground_surfaces()` treats house plus annex as built area, so no lawn is laid inside the annex. The GF presentation sheet and the site plan draw the annex rooms, walls, openings and furniture, SLIDEs, dashed shading and the computed title block.
- **villa_svg.py:** the GF plate shows the annex and its furniture, SLIDEs and dashed shading. Room labels now show net area, matching the DXF sheets. Site and section numbers are computed. Plates go to VILLA_OUT when it is set; otherwise to the current folder as before.
- **villa_load.py / villa_verify.py:** annex (AX) furniture is placed on and checked against the A-102/A-102P sheets. A-104 sheets are included only when RF has rooms. shower and shower_seat go on the fixtures layer. Output folder via `G.out_dir()`.
